answer: Ferrous Anchor Ledger. Each new agent identity must embed a unique hardware-rooted key whose first transaction routes through a public inlet: a challenge that requires 12 minutes of sequential memory-hard work before any action is accepted. The ledger records each key's lineage; clones deriving from one inlet share a decaying reputation tax, dropping rewards 40% per generation. Attackers pay full compute on every clone while the original anchor's yield stays fixed, so each marginal clone nets negative expected value. Harbored duplicates collapse under the tax within days.
